title: How the five supplied lists overlap, and availability by pattern
question: How do the overlapping memberships combine, how small are the overlaps that make some contrasts descriptive, and how does availability differ by exact pattern?
notes_text: Source: RFSD v3.1.0; lab aggregation of the foundation registry by exact five-list membership pattern and financial year. Each row is one pattern of the supplied lists (sanctioned, decree, residents, government strategic, presidential strategic); connected dots mark the lists a pattern belongs to, so rows are disjoint and their counts add up to the eligible population. Counts are eligible records in 2021; shares divide records with an original statement by eligible records in the pattern. Patterns with fewer than 50 records are shown in gray. Lists are fixed supplied files with overlaps, not dated designations. Descriptive.
reading: The five lists overlap in a handful of small patterns; only three patterns exceed 400 records, which is why most combined contrasts stay descriptive.
source_line: Foundation registry, lab aggregation by pattern
